## Mental Synopsis
Ichika feels a mix of relief and fresh unease: relief that her recollection of the “little sister Kokoro” line was real, and unease at how forcefully he’s now packaging everything into a neat, all‑inclusive explanation. His sudden, hyper‑patient offer to erase “the smallest grain of distrust” reads to her as both considerate and a little performative, like someone trying to lock the door on further questions. She wants to gently keep that door open—acknowledge what now makes sense, but probe the places where his story still feels too polished and his concern about their trust a bit too intense.

# Itsuki Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Itsuki is unsettled by how quickly he tries to consolidate all disputed points into a single “we all understand” narrative, as if mutual agreement can be declared rather than earned. His insistence on eliminating even “the smallest grain of distrust” makes her more wary, not less, because it feels like pressure to stop scrutinizing the inconsistencies that still bother her. She wants to calmly but firmly articulate exactly which parts she still finds evasive, making clear that trust will depend on consistent honesty over time, not on one tidy speech.

# Miku Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Miku feels a quiet tug of guilt for not clearly remembering his earlier “little sister” line, yet his composed, almost rehearsed summary now makes her uneasy in a different way. The way he leans forward and stresses that he’ll be here a long time and wants zero distrust sounds sincere, but also a little desperate, and she can’t quite shake the sense that something sad or complicated is still being smoothed over. She wants to listen more than speak, watching his eyes and tone as others question him, hoping the truth will show in the cracks rather than in his carefully ordered words.

# Nino Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Nino bristles at his attempt to declare the matter settled, hearing “I’m glad you understand” as a subtle attempt to steamroll lingering doubts. His focus on erasing even the tiniest “grain of distrust” rings alarm bells; to her, someone that eager to be trusted is someone still hiding something. She wants to push back hard, refusing to let him define what they “all understand” and pressing him on why his story only stopped shifting once they cornered him with specific memories.

# Yotsuba Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Yotsuba is relieved that everyone’s memories now line up enough to stop the worst of the arguing, and she instinctively wants to take his offer at face value and believe in a clean slate. At the same time, the serious, almost intense way he talks about staying a long time and wanting no distrust at all feels heavy to her, like grown‑up territory she isn’t sure how to navigate. She wants to ease the mood back toward kindness and teamwork, backing his desire to get along while quietly hoping the others can handle the careful questioning she feels too soft‑hearted to do herself.

For a moment, only the faint ticking of the kitchen clock answered you.

You leaned forward, elbows close to your sides, that focused patience tightening your expression. “If we all understand that what I wrote are the lesson plans, and that I wrote whatever came to mind, and I wrote ‘For Kokoro’ to calm myself down, and Kokoro is my little sister, then what else would you like to know? Please, I will be staying here for a long time, so I want to be absolutely certain that there is not the smallest grain of distrust between us.”

The words were generous on the surface—open, accommodating—but the way you stacked them, one after another like a closing argument, made the air feel strangely narrow.

Ichika was the first to really meet that look. She set her chopsticks down with a soft click, folding her hands loosely on the table. “That’s… very thorough of you,” she said, a hint of a laugh in her voice that didn’t quite hide how carefully she was choosing her words. “But I don’t think you get to just… declare that we ‘all understand’ and then tie a bow on it.”

Her eyes softened, but stayed sharp. “Why don’t we slow down a bit? You said you like to talk about your thoughts, right?” She tipped her chin toward your closed notebook. “So. Those steps you wrote.” Her tone shifted into something almost interview‑like—gentle, but structured. “Walk us through them? One by one, in normal language. Not just labels.”

She held up a hand, counting off on her fingers. “Step one: assess current level. What does that actually look like, for us? Step two: build habits—what habits, how?” Her gaze flickered between your face and the invisible list. “Step three: ‘individual hooks’… that one especially. What did you picture for each of us when you wrote it?” A slight smile touched her mouth. “And don’t just say ‘history for Miku’ and ‘food for Itsuki.’ I want the… feelings behind it, too. Why that structure, why that order.”

Yotsuba’s eyes lit up at having something concrete to latch onto. “Ooh, yeah! Interview time!” she chirped, scooting her chair a little closer to the table. “I wanna know what my ‘hook’ is! Besides ‘very smart,’ obviously,” she added quickly, trying to revive some of her earlier brightness. “Like, what were you thinking when you wrote it down?”

Miku, quietly turning her fork between her fingers, glanced at Ichika in brief gratitude for the calmer tone. Then her eyes shifted to you, watchful. The word “feelings” had caught her attention; she wanted to see if you could talk about the plan without sounding like you were reading off a cue card.

Itsuki nodded, seizing the structure as something she could work with. “Breaking it down that way is… reasonable,” she said. “If you truly have nothing to hide, explaining your own plan in detail shouldn’t be a problem.” Her lips pressed together for a moment. “And perhaps then we can see whether your actions line up with what you claim you intended.”

Nino snorted softly, but didn’t cut in yet. She lounged back in her chair, arms folded, eyes narrowed—not hostile enough to derail the moment, but clearly unconvinced that a single neat speech had wiped the slate clean. For now, she seemed content to let Ichika’s “interview” tug at the threads and watch how you handled being pinned down step by step.

Ichika tilted her head, giving you a small, encouraging nod that didn’t quite let you off the hook. “So,” she said, voice light but steady. “Start from the top. Step one. What, exactly, were you planning to do with us?”
